name: Basilique Marie-Reine-des-Apôtres de Mvolyé
subtitle: Minor basilica crowned with local hard-timber pillars and indigenous Bamun and granite artisanal elements.

facts.label: Consecrated
facts.value: 10 December 2006 (proclaimed minor basilica by Benedict XVI)

facts.label: Structure
facts.value: Supported by 12 massive columns of precious bubinga and moabi timbers

facts.label: Indigenous art
facts.value: Granite altar shaped like a traditional abbia gaming piece and Bamun-crafted bronze tabernacle

parts.text: A celebrated minor basilica situated atop Mvolyé hill in southern Yaoundé, on the grounds where German Pallottine missionaries led by Heinrich Vieter established the first Catholic mission in the area in 1901. Dedicated in 2006, the basilica is renowned for its bold African inculturation architecture: its expansive roof rests upon twelve monumental solid-wood pillars carved from indigenous bubinga and moabi tree trunks representing the apostles, accompanied by an altar carved from grey granite in the form of an ancient game token (abbia) and bronze reliefs fashioned after Bamun royal craft traditions.
